title: pilot-staging-gatekeeper-and-metric-axioms
summary: Working runbook for pilot staging gatekeeper: automated signals + manual review flow + a set of metric axioms to unify KPI computations across teams. Purpose: reduce ambiguity at pilot->rising-tide handoff and make automated gating reproducible.
body:
Context:
- Pilot will run in Dedicated-staging cluster (eu-west-1) with canary routing to 5% of pilot customers.
- This doc collects the gate criteria, the smoke test matrix, and a small library of "metric axioms" (how we compute numerator/denominator, smoothing, and alert sensitivity) so SRE/Product/Dev can speak the same language.

Why gatekeeper?
- We observed unclear roll decisions last quarter: different teams measured success differently which delayed rollouts.
- Gatekeeper = lightweight CI job + human review: automated checks run on pre-prod traces + telemetry then a short review call if any red signals.

Gatekeeper flow (high-level):
1) Preflight job runs nightly during pilot: pulls last 24h telemetry and runs signal checks.
2) If all checks pass -> auto-green for staged traffic increase (5% -> 15%).
3) If any check is amber -> create triage ticket (JIRA:PRODOPS-321) and assign to oncall + product owner.
4) If any check is red -> block rollout, notify exec oncall and pause traffic.

Staging environment requirements (must be true before gatekeeper runs):
- Staging mirrors committed config: same model version pinned, quantization profile = q4_0, cache warmup script ran.
- Isolation: no external prod keys, synthetic customer dataset used.
- Canary routing layer configured (traffic-split tag: pilot-2024-09).

Traffic allocation plan (pilot phases):
- Phase A (pilot initial): 0% -> 5% traffic for 48h
- Phase B (rising tide): 5% -> 15% for 72h
- Phase C (scale verification): 15% -> 50% with autoscale on; manual approval required for >50%
- Each step requires gatekeeper green or explicit product-ops approval.

Metric axioms (short, normative rules developers must follow):
1) Request success rate: define numerator as "responses with HTTP 200 and no user-facing error tag"; denominator = total requests that reached the model service (exclude client-side timeouts). Use 5-minute rolling window and 3-sample smoothing.
2) Latency p50/p95: measure server-side token-response time excluding network proxy; report both absolute ms and delta vs baseline. Baseline = last 7 days median for equivalent request class.
3) Cost per 1k requests: compute with token-units consumed * current unit-rate; include inference VM hour amortization for Dedicated pools. Use invoice-rate for currency conversion.
4) Quality regression: use seeded prompt-suite (prompt-suite id: ps-pilot-09) and compute metric = percent of prompts where top-ranked response drops below baseline quality score by >= 3 points.
5) Sample weighting: when computing cohort KPIs, weight by unique customer-monthly-active to avoid small-user churn spikes dominating pilot signals.

Smoke test matrix (run after each model push to staging):
- Test 1: end-to-end generation latency (small prompt, 32 tokens) -> expected p95 < 450ms.
- Test 2: streaming stability (10 parallel streams for 60s) -> no disconnects, <1% reconnect rate.
- Test 3: KV-cache hit rate (warmup scenario) -> >80% after warmup script.
- Test 4: Function-calling correctness (3 mapped functions) -> 100% stable call behavior on canonical inputs.
- Test 5: Auth & telemetry (request tags + billing fields) -> present on all spans.

Gatekeeper signals: automated checks to evaluate
- Stability: request success rate (5m window) >= 99.5%
- Latency: p95 delta <= +25% over baseline or absolute p95 <= 750ms
- Cost: estimated cost/1k requests delta <= +30% vs baseline (for pilot this is allowed but flagged)
- Quality: seeded prompt-suite pass rate >= 95%
- Observability: traces present for 99% of sampled requests and logs include model_version label

Triage rubric (quick guidance for human reviewers):
- Minor amber: single metric slightly outside thresholds but no customer impact -> document, continue, add mitigation ticket with owner.
- Major amber: two or more metrics outside thresholds or one critical regression (quality drop >7 points or success rate <98%) -> pause rollout, create P1 and lock traffic.
- Red: safety issue, data leak, or any customer-reported failure -> immediate rollback and incident page.

Checklist before manual approval for phase B->C:
- All gatekeeper signals green for 72h
- Acceptance signoff from product owner + SRE lead
- On-call schedule published for next 7 days
- Playbook (this doc) linked in the roll ticket

Open questions / notes to self:
- Do we need separate axioms for reranking endpoints? (Probably yes; quality metric calc differs)
- Where to land the standard prompt-suite (confluence v repo)? add to linked_artifacts.
- Sync with infra to ensure cost calc includes Dedicated amortization formula (INFR-882).

Appendix: quick command snippets
- Run preflight locally: python tools/gatekeeper/checks.py --window 24h --env staging --suite ps-pilot-09
- Force a smoke test run in CI: .ci/smoke/pilot-smoke.yml -> trigger via GH actions.

References:
- JIRA:PRODOPS-321 (pilot automation), JIRA:INFR-882 (cost accounting), PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-scripts/pull/47

---
This is a working doc. Expect frequent edits. Use comments inline rather than forking until we hit 'final' status.
